culprit_citations.quoted_text: From distributable earnings | (0.19) for the three months ended March 31, 2026
From return of capital | (0.11) for the three months ended March 31, 2026
Net investment income | 2.09% for the three months ended March 31, 2026

findings.detail: F16 treats total distributions as income-backed, but the filing identifies $0.11 per unit as return of capital in addition to $0.19 from distributable earnings.

rationale: Raw filing table 26 shows that the 2026 quarterly distribution is $0.30 per unit, split between $0.19 from distributable earnings and $0.11 from return of capital, while net investment income is $0.20 per unit and 2.09% of average net assets. Thus a total-distribution rate can legitimately exceed the income-yield heuristic because it includes an expressly disclosed return-of-capital component. The source supports the reported fields; the F16 comparison is inapplicable without distribution-composition scope.
